Theorem
[Uniqueness on bounded domains]

↗ thm:strong-maximum-principle-heat-equation ↗ thm:weak-maximum-principle-heat

1. ch2:2.3-thm-5\group Maximum Principles

For $g\in C(\Gamma _T)$ and $f\in C(U_T)$, there is at most one $u\in C_1^2(U_T)\cap C(\overline U_T)$ satisfying \[ (22)\qquad \begin{cases} u_t-\Delta u=f& \text{in }U_T,\\ u=g& \text{on }\Gamma _T. \end{cases} \]
Proof

↗ thm:weak-maximum-principle-heat

\sketch The difference $w$ of two solutions satisfies the homogeneous heat equation and vanishes on $\Gamma _T$. Apply the weak maximum principle to $w$ and $-w$.

□
